note: Town of La Pointe park on Madeline Island, about 6 miles from the ferry dock, beside Big Bay Lagoon; the Lake Superior beach is a short walk from the picnic shelter. Electric sites 34-55 (except 47A and 47B) are wooded with gravel pads; non-electric sites 1-27, 33, 47A and 47B suit tents, pop-ups and small trailers. Walk-in sites 28-32 and hike-in sites 56-61 are tent only; the booking filter shows which sites take a given rig length. Wi-Fi at the main office only. Dump station at the airport entrance on Big Bay Road ($5 donation). Distinct from Big Bay State Park to the south. --Claude
summary: Operator site (curl and rendered) and imagery read. Fees $45 electric confirmed (non-electric $35), 8 people / 2 vehicles per site; booking online (Premier Campground Management on the park's own site), 600-day window; facilities: pay showers, flush toilets, potable water, Wi-Fi at the office. No camping season is published (park 'Open year round'; water off 2026-10-28). WATERFRONT not waterfront -> coastal walk recommended: the loops are about 300-600 m from the park's own Lake Superior beach by park/local road, no highway or settlement between.
flags: WATERFRONT: stored 'not waterfront' -> recommend 'coastal walk'. Esri shows the loops (centre about 46.8195,-90.6788; east end about 46.8195,-90.6768) in forest on the NW side of Big Bay Lagoon; the Lake Superior beach at the lagoon mouth (about 46.8199,-90.6741) is roughly 300-600 m away by Big Bay Road and the park's own picnic/parking area. The operator: 'Access to the beach is just a short walk from the picnic shelter'. Only a local road and the park's own day-use area lie between; no highway, town, rail or residential strip. No site is on the water (lagoon side is wetland and forest, not open ground), so no lakefront. Electric sites 34-55 are sold by the night. Suggested waterfront_evidence: 'Esri 2026-11-16: loops 46.8195,-90.6788 in forest NW of Big Bay Lagoon; park's own Lake Superior beach at the lagoon mouth ~300-600 m by park/local road (operator: beach a short walk from the picnic shelter); no highway/town between -> coastal walk'.
